summary: @workoscalif/sudoku ships opaque 33 MB Go binaries executed during npm install, unrelated to the declared C source
details: The package's declared postinstall hook spawns vendor/gridgen-${process.platform}-${process.arch} on npm install. The arm64 vendored binaries are ~34–67 KB and consistent with the shipped native/gridgen.c source (symbols like _print_grid, _allowed, _count_solutions; no file, socket, or environment access). The x64 vendored binaries are 33 MB Go executables containing runtime symbols, GODEBUG, chacha8, /proc/self/cgroup, /proc/self/mountinfo, and time.Location — capabilities entirely absent from the C source the README presents as the only native code. vendor/gridgen-darwin-x64 and vendor/gridgen-linux-x64 are byte-identical (sha256 05b69666193e8fa719c37df22833bf36a120b15e2408a9ecd47e34f140a44420) and both contain Linux-only ELF/procfs strings, so the darwin-x64 file is a mislabeled Linux ELF rather than a Mach-O build. The x64 binaries are therefore an opaque payload masquerading as the advertised sudoku grid generator, executed on the installer's machine during npm install on any x64 Linux (or attempted darwin-x64) host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
